data.cultural_impact: The Hebrew name Ammiel is rooted in the rich cultural heritage of the ancient Israelites. The name carries the deep connection between God and his people, emphasizing the unity and communal spirit of ancient Israel. The name Ammiel may have been given as a reminder that God is ever-present within the community of believers and is a powerful expression of faith and belonging.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Ammiel lies in the profound message it conveys about God's relationship with his people. Ammiel reminds us that God is not just an individual's God, but also the God of the community, the God who walks among us as our collective protector, guide, and sustainer. This name invites us to reflect on our own relationships with both God and our fellow human beings, and to strive for unity and mutual support within the spiritual fellowship of the faith.

historical_references.reference: Ammiel, son of Netophah, was a Levite who accompanied Ezra to Jerusalem to help in the work of rebuilding the temple. (Ezra 8:9)
In the New Testament, Ammiel is the name given to a ruler of Judea who welcomes Herod Antipas to Jerusalem. (Matthew 14:1)
